digest: This week's research digest examines financial devices and institutional dynamics shaping Southern financial centres' position within global hierarchies. Antipode publishes new work on Ecuador's sovereign bonds as mechanisms of market discipline, while the Macroeconomics and Finance in Emerging Market Economies journal interrogates stablecoin adoption risks in the Franc Zone and dollarisation pressures. Complementing this are studies of India's distressed-asset market transformation under private equity ownership, the BRICS Synthetic Clearing Bridge as architecture for de-dollarisation, and how rating disciplines constrain multilateral development institutions like the AIIB. Reporting from Jeune Afrique documents South–South financial competition—Afreximbank versus Standard Bank in megaproject finance—and Airtel Money's entry into Northern capital markets, while concurrent moves by the African Union and Vietnam to launch independent rating agencies and advance financial-centre positioning reflect deliberate challenges to Northern valuation monopolies. Ethiopia's 2024 shift to interest-rate-based monetary policy and Kenya's opening of the Dangote IPO to domestic investors illustrate the institutional microstructures through which financial integration or autonomy emerges in lower-income economies.
